column1: # Suites deliberately outside CI, their mode, their reason, their ticket.
# mika#2761. ONE source of truth, ONE reader: scripts/check-suite-wiring.sh.
# THE RULE THIS FILE ENCODES
#   A test suite that lives in the tree must be REACHABLE from a workflow, or
#   be DECLARED here with a mode, a reason and a ticket. There is no third
#   state, and the empty state — present on disk, absent from CI, absent from
#   here — is what the lint refuses.
# This file holds the RESIDUE, not the census. The 70-odd suites CI does reach
# are not listed: for those the tree is already the source of truth — a workflow
# names them. Declaring them would create a second site to maintain for a fact
# already proven, and a registry you must edit on every CI rewiring is a
# registry that drifts. That is precisely the class of mika#2092, self-inflicted.
# `scripts/canonical-tokens.tsv` declares *all* its tokens because nothing else
# in the tree states a reader's tolerance; here CI *is* the source for "is it
# wired". The declarative principle applies to the ambiguous remainder only.
# `mode` IS A WIRE FORMAT, validated against a closed vocabulary
#   operator   the suite needs the outside world — network, a token, a live
#              service, a pid — or it is a deliberate measuring instrument.
#              Legitimately not a CI gate.
#   unwired    the suite runs offline, and nothing runs it. THE BACKLOG.
#              `grep -c unwired scripts/suite-wiring.tsv` is its size.
# A third state exists and is NEVER written here: a wired suite. Its proof is
# the workflow that names it, and the lint goes RED on an entry for a suite CI
# reaches — so an entry cannot outlive its reason. The gesture that makes an
# exception pointless (wiring the suite) is the gesture that makes it fail.
# The operator/unwired frontier is the discriminant of mika#1801: *does this
# script need the outside world?* That document states the machine cannot ask
# that question. So it does not: the HUMAN decides by filling the field, the
# MACHINE checks the form — mode in the vocabulary, reason non-empty, ticket
# present. Same discipline as the `tolérance` column of canonical-tokens.tsv.
# "Needs bwrap" is NOT "needs the outside world". ci.yml:133-149 already runs
# two real-sandbox suites on a hosted runner, on the stated ground that each
# "skips cleanly when bwrap is absent, so it is safe on a hosted runner". A
# suite that degrades to a skip is wirable; calling it `operator` would hide a
# backlog entry behind a word.
# POSITIVE POPULATION CONTROL (mika#2205, layer 2 of the mika#1801 taxonomy)
# The lint must not go green by looking at nothing. Measured 2026-10-18 on
# `0170f5cd`: 112 `*.sh`/`*.py` files under `scripts/` and
# `skills/bundled/_shared/`, of which 94 carry a suite prefix. The floor below
# leaves ~10% of room for legitimate deletions and catches a collapse of the
# enumeration — a renamed root, a changed prefix convention, a broken glob.
# Lowering it is allowed; doing so silently is not: say why in the commit.
# min-population: 85
# FORMAT: four TAB-separated columns, no header row.
#   path      repo-relative, exactly as the tree spells it
#   mode      operator | unwired
#   reason    why, in human words. An empty reason is the allowlist mika#2309
#             condemns: it says "skip me" and carries nothing else.
#   ticket    at least one `mika#<n>` — the ticket that gives the reason its
#             meaning. For `operator`, the one that established the deliberate
#             character. For `unwired`, the one that established the SUITE:
#             what it protects is what its absence from CI costs. The wiring of
#             the whole `unwired` column is tracked collectively by mika#2793,
#             whose work list is this file read through `grep unwired`.
scripts/measure-plan-header-coverage.sh
column3: Deliberate instrument, never a gate — Makefile:200 and CLAUDE.md both say so in those words. It reports a coverage ratio over the plan corpus; there is no threshold to fail on, and inventing one here would turn a measurement into a gate nobody chose.

column1: scripts/verify-dependabot-topology.sh
column3: Reads three real repositories through `gh api`, so it needs a cross-repo token CI does not carry. Its offline half is scripts/test-verify-dependabot-topology.sh, which fakes `gh` and replays both states.

column1: skills/bundled/_shared/tests/test_egress_relay_socket_and_env.sh
column3: 0600 relay socket, minimal relay launch environment, and reachability from a real bwrap pilot — point 3 is the one the canary cannot give. Skips cleanly when bwrap is absent, the precondition ci.yml:138 already accepts.

column1: skills/bundled/_shared/tests/test_rescue_fmt_clean.sh
column3: Pins that the rescue leaves a formatted tree rather than a diff the next flight must clean. Offline.

column1: skills/bundled/_shared/tests/test_sandbox_git_usable.sh
column3: git usable inside the pilot sandbox, plus the containment that bounds it. Builds its own worktrees and skips cleanly when bwrap is absent or the root is not a repository.

column1: skills/bundled/_shared/tests/test_sandbox_log_dir_bound.sh
column3: The pilot's session-log directory is writable from inside the sandbox while the incident-diagnosis surface stays out. Skips cleanly without bwrap, and skips its two /var/log/mika assertions when the host lacks that path.
